2026-12-15.title: Third Tuesday of Annunciation
2026-12-15.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
readings: Salvation is the gift of God
The kingdom of heaven has come near
2026-12-15.verse: This is the one of whom the prophet Isaiah spoke when he said, “The voice of one crying out in the wilderness: ‘Prepare the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.’”
theo: “By grace you have been saved through faith, and this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God.” Paul reminds us that we were dead through trespasses, and God, “rich in mercy”, made us alive with Christ. Salvation is gift; good works are the path God prepared for us to walk in.

John the Baptist appears in the wilderness: “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near.” People confess their sins and are baptised in the Jordan. Repentance is not earning grace; it is opening the door to it. This week is a good time for the sacrament of confession.
outline: Ask: what valley must be filled, what mountain made low in your life?
Salvation is God's gift, not our achievement.
John calls us to turn back to God.
Make straight paths through confession and charity.
live: Make your Christmas confession this week.
Settle one crooked matter: a debt, a lie, a quarrel.
2026-12-15.prayer: God, rich in mercy, you saved me by grace. Give me true repentance and help me prepare the way for your Son. Amen.
altar: The Holy Qurbana is the gift of God, not the result of our works. We come not because we are worthy, but because he who is rich in mercy invites us.

quick: We are saved by grace through faith.
2026-12-15.action: Make your Christmas confession this week.
2026-12-15.question: What crooked path must I straighten for the Lord?

family.explain: God loves us so much that he saves us as a gift. We do good things not to earn his love, but because we already have it.
family.intention: We pray for someone in our family who has gone far from God.
family.ask: Ask: “What good work has God prepared for us to do this week?”

pm.open: God, rich in mercy, you made us alive in Christ when we were dead in sin. Gather us in thanksgiving and make us ready to do the good works you have prepared for us. Amen.
share: Paul writes: but God, who is rich in mercy (Ephesians 2:4). Where have I seen God bring life out of death?
Do I sometimes think I must earn God's love?
John called for repentance (Matthew 3:2). What do I need to turn away from?
pm.resp: By grace we have been saved; thanks be to God.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim God's mercy to all who feel dead in sin.
For family members who have left the faith, that they may return.
For those battling addiction, that God's grace may raise them up.
For penitents preparing for Christmas confession, that they may experience God's mercy.
For all of us, that we may walk in the good works God has prepared.
pm.close: Lord God, you raised us with Christ by grace. Let us never boast of ourselves, but give thanks always, and walk in the good works you prepared for us. Amen.

illus: A father in Kollam had given up on his son, who had left home after years of drinking. One Christmas the son walked into the midnight Qurbana, thin and ashamed, and knelt at the back. After the Qurbana he went to confession. His father later said: “I had written him off. But God had not.”

homily: Dear friends, St Paul reminds the Ephesians where they came from: you were dead through the trespasses and sins in which you once lived (Ephesians 2:1). Not merely weak or sick, but dead. A dead person cannot raise himself.

Then come two of the most beautiful words in the Bible: but God. But God, who is rich in mercy, out of the great love with which he loved us even when we were dead through our trespasses, made us alive together with Christ; by grace you have been saved (Ephesians 2:4–5).

Paul insists: by grace you have been saved through faith, and this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God, not the result of works, so that no one may boast. For we are what he has made us, created in Christ Jesus for good works (Ephesians 2:8–10). We are not saved by good works, but we are saved for good works.

In the Gospel John the Baptist appears in the wilderness of Judea, proclaiming: repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near. People from Jerusalem and all Judea went out to him and were baptised in the Jordan, confessing their sins (Matthew 3:1–6).

John's message and Paul's message meet. Repentance is not our way of earning grace; it is the turning of the face towards the God who is already coming to meet us. The people confessed their sins because they hoped in mercy.

The word ‘but God’ is for every situation that looks dead: a marriage, a son who has left the Church, an addiction, a business failure. Let us bring these to the Lord this week, confess our part, and trust that God, rich in mercy, can make the dead alive. Amen.
kids: Children, John the Baptist told people to get ready for Jesus. Get your heart ready by saying sorry for your mistakes!

intro: Theme: “Prepare the way of the Lord.”
Saved by grace; called to repentance by John.

sub: Isaiah announced a highway for God.
q: A voice cries out: “In the wilderness prepare the way of the LORD, make straight in the desert a highway for our God.”
In those days John the Baptist appeared in the wilderness of Judea, proclaiming, “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near.”
points.apply: Make your Christmas confession this week.

sub: Pride must be humbled, despair lifted.
q: Every valley shall be lifted up, and every mountain and hill be made low; the uneven ground shall become level, and the rough places a plain. Then the glory of the LORD shall be revealed, and all people shall see it together.
This is the one of whom the prophet Isaiah spoke when he said, “The voice of one crying out in the wilderness: ‘Prepare the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.’”
points.apply: Settle one crooked matter this week.

sub: God gives a new heart and spirit.
q: A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you.
For the Son of Man came to seek out and to save the lost.
points.apply: Thank God for his mercy tonight.

concl: Grace comes first; repentance opens the door.
Prepare the way of the Lord.
